clinician.final_diagnosis: VBDS diagnosed in a patient presenting with cHL
clinician.trajectory_summary: A male patient in his 20s presented with jaundice, abdominal pain, nausea, intermittent fevers, and weight loss, along with bulky diffuse adenopathy and a lytic femur lesion. Initial workup revealed leucocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP). CT imaging showed diffuse lymphadenopathy, pulmonary nodules, hepatomegaly, and splenic hypodensities. Lymph node and medullary femur biopsies confirmed nodular sclerosing classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (cHL). Further investigations ruled out common infectious and autoimmune causes of inflammation and liver disease. A liver biopsy showed acute cholangitis with small bile duct obliteration. The patient's clinical course was complicated by neutropenic infections and pneumonitis, with the latter treated with high-dose steroids. While direct genetic confirmation of UBA1 mutation or specific bone marrow findings for vacuoles were not reported, the constellation of systemic inflammatory symptoms, elevated inflammatory markers, specific inflammatory organ involvement (cholangitis, pneumonitis), and exclusion of alternative inflammatory conditions, alongside the confirmed cHL, supports the diagnosis of VEXAS syndrome (VBDS) in this patient.
